scope: Read-only extraction from completed r115 T20 logs; no build, edit or rerun.
profile: debug_assertions=true (dev profile); Apple M1 Pro, 32 GiB, macOS 27.2 (26B123)

thresholds.requirement: p95 main-thread save-related work < 50 ms on same 43,200-occurrence fixture; hardware and sample count recorded
first history page p95 < 30 ms via real query path
opening first history page does not deserialize every report; benchmark memory/latency/db-size
reproducible synchronous UI save block < 50 ms

thresholds.source: TASKS.md:37 smoothness release requirement (native acceptance not offline frame benchmark)
thresholds.requirement: smooth scrolling; 60 Hz frame budget is indicative only, not an offline gate

automation-ui-save-block.note: 1888 ms synchronous block is a legacy automation-perf failure. Fresh live standalone save cases pass but are single samples; live p95 is unmeasured.

render-frame.note: Offline in-memory debug frames, not native or live. Steps/Project/Topic exceed 16.7 ms indicative budget; this cannot reject or accept current live/native smoothness by itself.

legacy-path-save-p95.note: These are legacy attach_storage full-load/save numbers, not the current live worker path. They remain a real failure of the benchmarked legacy path. Applying them as current live T14 failure would be wrong.

legacy-path-first-page.status: LEGACY_ONLY (occ render indicative pass; larger fixtures over audit-proposed 30 ms; strict query gate unmeasured)
legacy-path-first-page.note: Legacy harness/UI render wall only. It does not measure the live indexed query path or live p95.

legacy-path-lazy-body.note: Legacy load read every report body in this harness and presentation bytes are synthetic. This is a coverage gap for live lazy-body acceptance, not proof the current live path deserializes every report.

persistence-perf (all six modes).backend: legacy full load/save; no ordered live worker

render-perf.backend: offline in-memory mock render; no storage/live worker

live_gate_status.reason: Each live run reports one headless sample per case. Single samples cannot establish p95 under the TASK target; none of these is a live p95 measurement.

live_coverage_gap: No live benchmark currently repeats save/history interactions >=30 times through LiveStartup to report p95 on the 43,200 fixture.
Existing --qa-persistence-perf and --qa-automation-perf use attach_storage (legacy) and cannot stand in for live T14/T15.
No live product counter proves bodies are not read on first history page; presentation bytes in the legacy harness are synthetic.
A live harness should report p50/p95/p99/max, sample count, hardware/profile, DB size, peak RSS, body bytes read, and exact constructor (Some(LiveStartup)).
limitations: Persistence benchmark logs are dev profile and use the benchmark fixture harness; they do not by themselves prove the live worker main-thread path.
Warm save sample counts are 5-20; a stable p95 requires >=30 as the logs state.
Presentation bytes are synthetic; no product body-read counter exists.
History render wall is not a query-only span.
Offline render-frame numbers are not native scrolling acceptance.
Inventory mode has fixture metadata but no save/history timing run.
